---
title: "How do I get quartiles, an IQR, and a five-number summary?"
---

## The question

How do I get quartiles, an IQR, and a five-number summary?

## What to check and do

1. Use numeric data. 2. Calculate quantiles and interquartile range. 3. State the quartile convention when precision or small samples matter.

## Worked example: mtcars

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("mtcars")
answer <- ru_apply("five_number", data=d, x="mpg")
stopifnot(answer$IQR>0, length(answer$quantile)==5)
```

The IQR describes the middle half of the fuel-economy measurements. R's quantile() and fivenum() can use different conventions for the quartiles.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("five_number", data=your_data, x="numeric_column")
```

For outliers, check the boxplot convention (1.5 × IQR) rather than calling every extreme number an error.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("five_number")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
